description.purpose: The container this person's applications are instantiated into. It ships empty and open: no cells, no ports, no contract of its own. An APP is a specific composition and specific code that came out of a build order -- a derived template in the library, tagged `app` -- and what it produces is a VIEW. It is not a channel: a channel is how the person is reached, an app is something the person's screen shows. It stands beside `./channels` and `./assistants` rather than inside either, because an app belongs to the PERSON: it outlives a generation swap the way a channel does, and two of the person's agents may hold views on the same screen it writes to.
description.use_when: Never on its own -- it travels with the member level. One app is one node instantiated into this container at the name it is known by (`colony-view`, a project board, a day plan), and an app is instantiated, never shipped. AN APP HAS NO PORT AND NO SURFACE OF ITS OWN: it writes views onto a display, and the display is a channel of this same member. Whatever authentication stands in front of that screen stands in front of the app; giving an app a port would be a second front door nobody counted. TRANSIT, and since 1.6.2 it is wider in both directions. OUT, from an app up into the level: `view` (one picture towards a screen, carried on by the level's own `./apps -> ./channels` edge, which is guarded on a non-empty `context.channel`, so the app's OWN outbound edge is where the screen is named -- a literal in one edge, because an app is deliberately display-blind), `error`, and -- when the app offers a tool -- `tool_result` (its answer to a call the surface made) and `tool_schemas` (its offer on the way into the menu). The level restamps the last two into `in_tool` and `in_menu` on its own two edges out of this container, exactly the way the memory's answer is restamped (GH #552), and the round ends where it began. IN, from the level down into an app: `event` (somebody acted on a view this app owns) and `receipt` (a write this app made was refused), and, for an app that LISTENS, the three observer lanes of the person -- `turn` (the screened turn of a channel conversation), `answer` (what an assistant replied on that channel) and `partial` (an interim transcript of a voice channel). All of them keep their lane name on the way down, because which inbound lane an app has is the app's business and the per-app edge is what names it. WHO DRAWS WHAT (ruling 2026-09-05): the LEVEL ships the declaration of the observer lanes -- they are named in the member's own contract with `at: ["./apps"]`, which is what makes the member a mandatory hop for anything carrying them from outside -- plus the level-side half of `view`, `error`, `event`, `receipt` and the two restamp edges out of this container. Every edge INTO this container on an observer lane, and the pair that binds one app to it by name, is drawn by the MUTATION that installs that app: whoever listens orders it, the way a voice channel is told `emit_partials` by whoever wants partials. A member with no listening app therefore carries no observer edge and dead-letters nothing, and a second installation redraws the same member-side edges without doubling them, because an identical edge is held once. AND WHAT PASSES THROUGH: the tool CALL (`tool`), the menu tick (`schemas`) and the OBSERVED answer of the generation's own tool hive (`tool_result`) do not stop here at all. They are v-lanes (ADR-0020) that end on connect points the app declares for itself, and this container is transparent to them because it carries no contract of its own.
description.not_in_scope: No ports, for the same load-bearing reason ./assistants and ./channels declare none: a sealed hive refuses exactly the endpoints an app instantiation needs (hive_port_boundary), and the pairing edge between this container and an app below it is such an endpoint. No slot: GH #285's slot governs an address that does not exist, and this container does exist, so the declared unbound word could never fire -- see unbound_slot_behaviour in crates/meclaw-colony/src/colony.rs, which steps aside as soon as the target is a registered hive scope. No params.contract either: this container is wired by its own level the moment the member is instantiated, so mutation::hive_contract::check_lane_doors sees a WIRED hive from birth (hive_path_is_wired) and would then owe a door inside for every declared accepts lane -- and a member with no app yet is a legitimate state, and the ordinary one. No cells. And no view of its own: a container holds apps, and the views are drawn one level down, by the app. Prose is the smallest KIND of view (GH #455), not a view an agent has for free -- an agent's `answer` carries `messages[]` and no `view_id`, and the screen refuses it as `invalid_view` (GH #597), so a paragraph on a screen is written by a producer of views like every other view.
